2021_196_principal_s_report_june_2021.paragraph: Principal's report presented to the Troy Board of Education on June 23, 2021 covering the International Academy's three campuses. It reports successful graduation ceremonies at West, Okma and East, and an IB examination session held April 29 through May 20 in which 326 students sat as full Diploma Program candidates, described as 94 percent of the graduating class. The report also sets the 2021-22 return-to-school calendar, announces an IB evaluation visit for November 10 through November 12, and summarizes a staff survey in which all three campuses chose Culture as the school goal to pursue next year.
2021_196_principal_s_report_june_2021.page:
Overview
Slide-style principal's report for the International Academy, presented at the Troy School District Board meeting of June 23, 2021. It covers end-of-year results, the coming IB evaluation, the 2021-22 opening calendar, a restructured school improvement committee, the four school goals, and verbatim staff survey comments.

Graduation
Ceremonies are reported as a success at all three campuses:

| Campus | Date | Location and time |
| --- | --- | --- |
| West | Wednesday, May 26 | Lakeland HS Fieldhouse, 7:00pm |
| Okma | Thursday, June 3 | BHHS Athletic Field, 7:00pm |
| East | Saturday, June 5 | DTE, 12:30pm |

IB examinations (April 29 to May 20)
The session is reported as a success. There were 326 full Diploma Program candidates, stated as 94 percent of the graduating class; 13 of those students will have one or more exams graded on the non-exam route because of quarantine or other illness. Another 18 were course candidates attempting HL credit, 1 student opted to return and take exams in November, and 8 students withdrew from all IB exams.

IB evaluation visit
Scheduled Wednesday, November 10 through Friday, November 12.

Return to school
Thursday, August 12 for new student orientation, new teacher orientation, and schedule pickup with school photos; Monday, August 16 for staff professional development; Tuesday, August 17 as the first day of school for students; Friday, August 27 no school.

Tri-Campus School Improvement Committee
The report proposes reinstituting a tri-campus School Improvement Committee that is both school wide and campus specific. Its responsibilities would be to prepare for IB evaluation visits, meet state professional development requirements, and develop professional development for staff.

School goals
Instruction: instruction will be engaging, innovative, student-centered and inquiry based, with the goal of promoting and supporting effective and innovative pedagogy in the classroom. Curriculum: the curriculum will be in full alignment with the standards of the International Baccalaureate Middle Years and Diploma Programs plus state standards, with interdisciplinary units fully implemented and assessed at all levels, a goal of two units per year for MYP, one each semester. Culture: the culture will balance the social, emotional and physical health of the community and embrace both commonalities and individuality, with goals to build capacity as a community cultivating a global culture of acceptance and inclusion and to foster a culture of service learning. Assessment: assessments will fairly evaluate diverse abilities, with formative assessment used for practice and feedback and summative assessment emphasizing mastery, and a goal of defining and aligning the assessment philosophy and policy within departments and school wide.

Staff survey
Asked which school goal to engage in for the 2021-22 school year, all three campuses chose Culture. Comments cite the need to rebuild culture after a year of uncertainty, student transition back to full face-to-face instruction, continued social-emotional support, and the view that culture is the foundation on which the other goals rest. Suggested secondary goals center on rethinking assessment, focusing on the Diploma Program, analyzing which pandemic-era instructional methods worked, and refining new DP curricula. Practices staff want to carry forward include asynchronous days, Canvas for organizing and collecting assignments, one-to-one device access, the House system and house competitions, the Open House video, and flexible time management. Staff also identified pre-COVID features they could do without, naming intense workload and stress levels and in-person conferences.

Mission statement
The report closes with the International Academy mission: through the International Baccalaureate program, instilling cultural appreciation and global citizenship while promoting personal development and a passion for learning.
2021_196_principal_s_report_june_2021.verbose:
Principal's report for the International Academy delivered to the Troy School District Board of Education at its June 23, 2021 meeting. The document is a slide deck covering the close of the 2020-21 school year and planning for 2021-22 across the Academy's three campuses, West, Okma and East.

Graduation. All three ceremonies are reported as a success. West held graduation Wednesday, May 26 at the Lakeland HS Fieldhouse at 7:00pm. Okma held graduation Thursday, June 3 at the BHHS Athletic Field at 7:00pm. East held graduation Saturday, June 5 at DTE at 12:30pm.

IB examinations. The exam window ran April 29 through May 20 and is likewise reported as a success. There were 326 full Diploma Program candidates, stated in the report as 94 percent of the graduating class. Of those, 13 students will have one or more of their exams graded on the non-exam route because of quarantine or other illness. A further 18 students sat as course candidates attempting HL credit. One student opted to return and take exams in November, and 8 students withdrew from all IB exams.

IB evaluation visit. The Academy will host an IB evaluation visit Wednesday, November 10 through Friday, November 12.

Return to school calendar. Thursday, August 12 is set for New Student Orientation, New Teacher Orientation, and Schedule Pickup and School Photos. Monday, August 16 is staff professional development. Tuesday, August 17 is the first day of school for students. Friday, August 27 is a no school day.

Tri-Campus School Improvement Committee. The report calls for reinstituting a tri-campus School Improvement Committee that operates both school wide and campus specific. Its stated responsibilities are to prepare for IB evaluation visits, address state professional development requirements, and develop professional development for staff.

School goals. Four goal areas are set out with accompanying statements.

Instruction. The instruction of the International Academy will be engaging, innovative, student-centered and inquiry based. The goal is to promote and support effective and innovative pedagogy in the classroom.

Curriculum. The curriculum of the International Academy will be in full alignment with the standards of the International Baccalaureate Middle Years and Diploma Programs in addition to state standards. The goal is that interdisciplinary units will be fully implemented and assessed at all levels, with a target of two units per year for MYP, one each semester.

Culture. The culture of the International Academy will balance the social, emotional and physical health of the community, and will embrace and value commonalities and individuality. Two goals are stated: continue to build capacity as a community that cultivates a global culture encouraging acceptance and inclusion, and foster and support a culture of service learning.

Assessment. Assessments will fairly evaluate the unique and diverse abilities and knowledge base of all students. Formative assessments will be used to strengthen skills and provide practice and feedback during the learning process, while summative assessments will emphasize mastery of the skills and content knowledge students have had an opportunity to learn. The goal is to define and align the assessment philosophy and policy within departments and as a school.

Staff survey and conversations, primary goal. Asked which school goal they would most like to engage in for the 2021-22 school year, all three campuses want to pursue Culture. Quoted staff responses include the observation that after a year of uncertainty the culture at IA will need rebuilding because students missed out on much of what makes the Academy distinctive; that IA has excellent educators who will adapt curriculum and instruction to make up for material not covered, but that the most important factors are the cultural pieces, including the culture of commitment to excelling, the culture derived from the Academy's international grounding, and the culture of interpersonal relationships many students have not been able to form; that culture is what students will be looking forward to when they return to full face-to-face instruction in the fall; that staff want to continue guiding students to succeed with the rigor of the IB program; that students and staff face a difficult transition back to real school and will need help balancing physical, emotional, educational and life stressors, with continued focus on SEL rather than a return to business as usual; that culture work is never done and there is much to do before changing priorities, since students will struggle to readjust next fall and supporting that transition should be the greatest priority; and that culture is the foundation upon which the others are built.

Staff survey, secondary goals. Responses on a secondary goal emphasize assessment and curriculum. Staff noted that the year forced a rethinking of assessment, with more creativity and less grade-driven work that was healthy for staff and students, and that high quality authentic assessments that do not overwhelm should continue. Working with digital assessments allowed work outside the box of what a typical summative and formative assessment looks like, prompting a desire to reevaluate assessment style going forward. Other comments call for spending time focusing on the Diploma Program; for more focus on in-person instruction after a year and a half on Zoom; for space and time to analyze which instructional methods introduced during the year worked and how they might improve overall instruction; for continued curriculum improvement, noting that large curricular hurdles were cleared during the year and that some choices favored ease during a stressful time over better curricular choices that now need correction; and for retaining classroom technologies, particularly methods that allowed more immediate feedback than traditional approaches, with interest in using them to differentiate assignments and assessments or to create a semi-self-paced course allowing more personal preference and interest. Additional responses ask for consistency between departments regarding assessment or a school-wide grading and percentage policy for tests, note that some teachers sit at polar ends of the assessment spectrum and that the whole staff should discuss the topic, and observe that new DP curricula in several subjects would benefit from extra time to iron out wrinkles.

Practices to carry forward and new ideas. Staff suggested exploring how asynchronous days could work, based on feedback gathered from numerous freshmen and sophomores met with during second semester, on the grounds that students and staff work very hard and would benefit from set-aside time. Continuing to use Canvas to organize and to an extent collect assignments was cited as useful, as was using Canvas to cut down on paper and communicate with absent students. Staff asked for easy and consistent student access to a device in class, describing one-to-one as a goal, and expressed enthusiasm for the House system, friendly house competitions and team building, more field trips after a year indoors, and connecting alumni with students. The Open House video was praised, and the picnic was reported to be better without grilling and with a focus on fun activities. Staff also valued professional consideration of time management, with flexibility to leave when not teaching or meeting described as crucial to mental health and to fulfilling work and home obligations, noting a high level of trust during the year that the job would get done.

Aspects of pre-COVID school life to do without. Staff named the intense workload and high levels of stress before COVID as detrimental to student and staff health, calling for additional and focused or protected time, and suggested that in-person conferences may not be necessary.

Additional comments. Staff asked that more teachers understand program expectations beyond their own disciplines, and suggested a workshop or professional development session on Canvas functionality since its many features can be confusing or unobvious to new users. Closing comments thank the principal for support and grace during a difficult year and for seeking staff input, express anticipation for the new school year, and state that culture and instruction are key to next year's success, with investment there also taking care of curriculum and assessments.

Mission. The report closes with the Academy's mission statement: the International Academy community, through the International Baccalaureate program, instills cultural appreciation and global citizenship while promoting personal development and a passion for learning.
